blocks.zh: 無菌充填系統設計案例研究（第一部分）
blocks.en: Aseptic Filling System Design Case Studies (Part 1)

blocks.zh: 本章學習目標
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解如何將產品特性（黏度、氧敏感性、剪切敏感性、起泡性）直接轉化為充填設備設計要求
blocks.en: Understand how product characteristics (viscosity, oxygen sensitivity, shear sensitivity, foaming tendency) translate directly into filling equipment design requirements

blocks.zh: 掌握小容量針劑（Case 1：預充填注射器）與大容量針劑（Case 2：瓶裝液體）的設計差異與決策邏輯
blocks.en: Grasp the design differences and decision logic between small volume parenterals (Case 1: prefilled syringe) and large volume parenterals (Case 2: liquid in a bottle)

blocks.zh: 學習如何透過結構化的需求矩陣，系統性比較 PP、RPP、TP、DP 四種充填技術的適用性
blocks.en: Learn how to use a structured requirements matrix to systematically compare the suitability of four filling technologies: PP, RPP, TP and DP

blocks.zh: 了解生產規模（批次大小、活動策略、IPC 選擇）如何影響充填線設計與年產量估算
blocks.en: Understand how production scale (batch size, campaign strategy, IPC selection) affects filling line design and annual output estimates

blocks.zh: 21.1 Case 1: Small Volume Parenteral — Liquid in a Syringe (預充填注射器案例)
blocks.en: 21.1 Case 1: Small Volume Parenteral — Liquid in a Syringe

blocks.zh: 原文內容 Original Text
blocks.en: Original Text

blocks.zh: 導師解析 Tutorial Commentary
blocks.en: Tutorial Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 產品特性驅動設計決策
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Product Characteristics Drive Design Decisions

blocks.zh: Case 1 的關鍵設計驅動因素有三個：
blocks.en: Case 1 has three key design drivers:

blocks.zh: 氧敏感性 (Oxygen-sensitive)：必須在充填關閉站導入惰性氣體（氮氣），以維護產品品質。這直接影響充填機的站點設計。
blocks.en: Oxygen-sensitive: Inert gas (nitrogen) must be introduced at the filling and closing station to protect product quality. This directly affects the station design of the filling machine.

blocks.zh: 剪切敏感性 (Shear-sensitive)：單株抗體 (monoclonal antibody, mAb) 蛋白質結構脆弱，高剪切力會造成蛋白質變性，直接排除旋轉活塞泵 (RPP) 的選用。
blocks.en: Shear-sensitive: The protein structure of a monoclonal antibody (mAb) is fragile, and high shear forces can denature it, so the rotary piston pump (RPP) is ruled out immediately.

blocks.zh: 起泡性 (Foaming Tendency)：要求充填曲線（加速、停止控制）精心設計，並採用潛針充填 (diving needle)，防止泡沫污染。
blocks.en: Foaming tendency: The filling profile (acceleration and stop control) must be carefully designed, and a diving needle should be used to prevent foam contamination.

blocks.zh: 注意：雖然本產品非高毒性，但廠商主動選擇隔離器 (isolator)，理由是「提升無菌保證」——這正是決策層級 #1 無菌保證 (Sterility Assurance) 優先於商業考量的示範。
blocks.en: Note: Although this product is not highly potent, the vendor proactively chose an isolator, with the rationale of "increasing sterility assurance". This is a textbook example of decision hierarchy #1, sterility assurance, taking priority over commercial considerations.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明
blocks.en: Analogy

blocks.zh: 想像你在煮一道很容易起泡的湯（比如豆漿）。你不能大火猛衝——必須用小火慢加熱，鍋緣輕輕倒入，避免攪拌過度。充填單株抗體也是同樣的道理：充填針的下降速度、充填起始位置、停止曲線都必須像廚師一樣精細控制，才能避免起泡和蛋白質損傷。
blocks.en: Imagine cooking a soup that foams easily (soy milk, for example). You cannot bring it to a rolling boil; you have to heat it gently, pour it in along the edge of the pot, and avoid over-stirring. Filling a monoclonal antibody follows the same principle: the descent speed of the filling needle, the starting fill position and the stop profile all have to be controlled as carefully as a chef would, to avoid foaming and protein damage.

blocks.zh: 練習思考 Practice Questions
blocks.en: Practice Questions

blocks.zh: 為什麼「非高毒性」的產品，廠商仍選擇隔離器而非 RABS？這個決策反映了哪個設計優先級？
blocks.en: Why did the vendor still choose an isolator rather than RABS for a product that is "not highly potent"? Which design priority does this decision reflect?

blocks.zh: 如果未來要在同一條線上充填不耐剪切的不同 mAb，旋轉活塞泵是否可行？請說明理由。
blocks.en: If different shear-sensitive mAbs are to be filled on the same line in the future, is a rotary piston pump viable? Explain your reasoning.

blocks.zh: 21.1.2 Case 1: Container–Closure Characteristics (容器密封系統特性)
blocks.en: 21.1.2 Case 1: Container–Closure Characteristics

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — 巢式預充填系統的設計細節
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Design Details of the Nested Prefilled System

blocks.zh: Case 1 採用巢式 (nested) 預充填注射器，每個設計細節都牽動充填機的特定子系統：
blocks.en: Case 1 uses nested prefilled syringes, and every design detail affects a specific subsystem of the filling machine:

blocks.zh: Nest 規格（160 支 / 盤）：直接決定充填頭的排列數量（fill lanes）及 X/Y 方向的運動需求。
blocks.en: Nest specification (160 syringes per tray): Directly determines the number of filling heads (fill lanes) and the X/Y motion requirements.

blocks.zh: Tub 高度（97 mm）：影響蓋膜 (lid) 與內襯 (liner) 的移除站設計，甚至決定是否需要機器人手臂。
blocks.en: Tub height (97 mm): Affects the design of the lid and liner removal station, and can even determine whether a robotic arm is needed.

blocks.zh: 容器密封完整性 (CCI)：必須在開發階段即確認，確保整個運輸鏈（包括冷藏）維持無菌密封。
blocks.en: Container closure integrity (CCI): Must be confirmed during development to ensure that a sterile seal is maintained throughout the entire transport chain (including cold storage).

blocks.zh: 頂空維護 (Headspace Maintenance) 需求直接引發一個設計問題：是否需要 100% 線上頂空檢測？這將影響充填速率與設備選型。
blocks.en: The headspace maintenance requirement directly raises a design question: is 100% in-line headspace inspection needed? This will affect the filling rate and equipment selection.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 供應商圖號的重要性
blocks.en: Key Point — The Importance of Supplier Drawing Numbers

blocks.zh: 表格中大量引用「Supplier Name, Drawing #XXX」，這不是形式主義。每個圖號代表精確的尺寸公差，直接影響分料碗 (sorting bowl)、軌道、插柱站的設計。CDMO 在早期就要鎖定這些資料——後期更改供應商或規格，可能導致整個充填機需要重新改裝。
blocks.en: The table frequently cites "Supplier Name, Drawing #XXX", and this is not mere formality. Each drawing number represents precise dimensional tolerances that directly affect the design of the sorting bowl, the tracks and the stoppering (plunger insertion) station. A CDMO needs to lock down this information early; changing the supplier or specification later may require the entire filling machine to be retrofitted.

blocks.zh: 如果廠商決定改用 200 支 / 盤的 nest，會對充填機設計產生哪些影響？
blocks.en: If the vendor decides to switch to a 200-syringe nest, what impact would this have on the filling machine design?

blocks.zh: 「氣泡大小不重要」的判斷依據是什麼？什麼情況下氣泡大小會變成關鍵設計參數？
blocks.en: What is the basis for the judgment that "bubble size is not important"? Under what circumstances would bubble size become a critical design parameter?

blocks.zh: 21.1.3 Case 1: Specific Filling Requirements — Headspace & Deaeration (充填頭空間與除氣要求)
blocks.en: 21.1.3 Case 1: Specific Filling Requirements — Headspace & Deaeration

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — 氮氣充入時機的設計邏輯
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Design Logic for the Timing of Nitrogen Gassing

blocks.zh: 惰性氣體（氮氣）的施加時機是一個「越晚越好」的設計原則：
blocks.en: For the application of inert gas (nitrogen), the design principle is "the later, the better":

blocks.zh: 在關閉站施加（gassing during closing）：這是本案例的選擇。氮氣在插柱瞬間充入頂空，排除最後一段空氣，效果最直接。
blocks.en: Gassing during closing: This is the choice made in this case. Nitrogen is introduced into the headspace at the moment of stopper insertion, displacing the last of the air, which is the most direct approach.

blocks.zh: 充填前或充填中施加：適用於對氧極度敏感的產品（如某些脂質體），但會增加設備複雜度及氮氣消耗。
blocks.en: Gassing before or during filling: Suitable for products that are extremely oxygen-sensitive (such as certain liposomes), but it adds equipment complexity and nitrogen consumption.

blocks.zh: 「充填前先抽真空排氣，再充入氮氣」的組合設計（本案即如此），是業界針對氧敏感注射器最常見的解決方案。
blocks.en: The combined design of "evacuating before filling, then gassing with nitrogen" (as in this case) is the most common industry solution for oxygen-sensitive syringes.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 未來彈性的前瞻設計
blocks.en: Key Point — Forward-Looking Design for Future Flexibility

blocks.zh: 文中特別注記：「未來若改用矽膠游離塞塞 (silicone-free stopper) 的塑膠注射器，真空短通氣管可能變得重要。」這是 Guide 全書一貫的精神——設計當下的需求，同時為未來留下升級空間，避免日後因設備限制喪失產品多樣性。
blocks.en: The text specifically notes: "If plastic syringes with silicone-free stoppers are used in the future, the vacuum short vent tube may become important." This reflects the consistent philosophy of the whole Guide: design for today's requirements while leaving room for future upgrades, so that equipment limitations do not later cost you product variety.

blocks.zh: 如果同一條線未來要充填一個對氧「極度」敏感（<0.1% O₂）的產品，目前「gassing during closing only」的設計是否足夠？需要增加哪些站點？
blocks.en: If the same line is to fill an "extremely" oxygen-sensitive product (<0.1% O₂) in the future, is the current "gassing during closing only" design sufficient? What additional stations would be needed?

blocks.zh: 21.1.4 Case 1: Multi-container / Multi-volume / Multi-product Flexibility (多容器／多體積／多產品彈性)
blocks.en: 21.1.4 Case 1: Multi-container / Multi-volume / Multi-product Flexibility

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — CDMO 平台設計的彈性思維
blocks.en: Core Concepts — A Flexible Mindset for CDMO Platform Design

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 而言，單一產品設計的充填線幾乎沒有商業意義。Case 1 展示了「多產品平台設計」的系統性思考：
blocks.en: For a CDMO, a filling line designed for a single product makes almost no commercial sense. Case 1 demonstrates systematic thinking about a "multi-product platform design":

blocks.zh: 容器彈性：從玻璃注射器到塑膠注射器，再到卡匣式容器——每一個變化都可能要求新的去靜電裝置、真空插柱能力或感測充填 (sensor filling)。
blocks.en: Container flexibility: From glass syringes to plastic syringes to cartridges, each change may require new static elimination devices, vacuum stoppering capability or sensor filling.

blocks.zh: 充填體積彈性：0.2 mL（底端能力）到 3 mL，跨越 15 倍的體積範圍，不是每種泵都能優雅應對。
blocks.en: Fill volume flexibility: From 0.2 mL (lower-end capability) to 3 mL, a 15-fold volume range, which not every pump type can handle gracefully.

blocks.zh: 充填技術彈性：同一機台底座 (machine base) 能否容納不同泵型（如 RPP + PP 並存），必須在初始設計時就決定——事後追加幾乎等於重建。
blocks.en: Filling technology flexibility: Whether the same machine base can accommodate different pump types (for example, RPP and PP side by side) must be decided at the initial design stage; adding them afterwards is almost equivalent to rebuilding.

blocks.zh: 這就像餐廳設計廚房：你現在只做義大利麵，但你已知三年後要加入壽司和烤肉。如果從一開始就預留了煤氣管線位置、排風管道、冷藏分區，未來擴展只需要安裝設備；若沒有預留，則需要打牆重裝——成本是原來的十倍。CDMO 的充填線設計也是如此。
blocks.en: It is like designing a restaurant kitchen: you only make pasta today, but you already know that sushi and grilled meat will be added in three years. If you reserve space for gas lines, exhaust ducts and refrigerated zones from the start, future expansion only requires installing equipment; if you do not, walls have to be torn down and rebuilt at ten times the original cost. The same applies to CDMO filling line design.

blocks.zh: 若未來要在這條線上充填 0.2 mL 的 mAb，哪種充填技術最適合？為什麼 DP（滾動膜片泵）可能被排除？
blocks.en: If 0.2 mL of mAb is to be filled on this line in the future, which filling technology is most suitable? Why might DP (rolling diaphragm pump) be ruled out?

blocks.zh: 從「巢式玻璃注射器」改為「塑膠注射器」時，設計上需要增加哪兩項主要能力？
blocks.en: When changing from "nested glass syringes" to "plastic syringes", which two main capabilities need to be added to the design?

blocks.zh: 21.1.5 Case 1: Anticipated Batch Sizes and Operating Practices (批次規模與生產操作規劃)
blocks.en: 21.1.5 Case 1: Anticipated Batch Sizes and Operating Practices

blocks.zh: 公式與計算 — 年產量估算框架
blocks.en: Formulas and Calculations — Framework for Estimating Annual Output

blocks.zh:
年可用工時 = 365 天 × 24 h × 設備效率 (70-80%)
           ≈ 365 × 24 × 0.75 = 6,570 小時

每批充填時間 = 批次充填數量 ÷ 充填速率
活動間換線 = 32 小時
批次間換線 = 4 小時

以 1 mL fill, 10-lane filler 為例：
100 L 批次 = 100,000 支注射器
若充填速率 = 400 支/min → 約 4.2 小時/批

5 批活動 = 5 × 4.2h 充填
           + 4h × 4 批次間換線
           + 32h 活動換線
           ≈ 85 小時 / 活動
blocks.en:
Available hours per year = 365 days × 24 h × equipment efficiency (70-80%)
           ≈ 365 × 24 × 0.75 = 6,570 hours

Filling time per batch = batch fill quantity ÷ filling rate
Campaign changeover = 32 hours
Batch-to-batch changeover = 4 hours

Example with a 1 mL fill, 10-lane filler:
100 L batch = 100,000 syringes
If filling rate = 400 syringes/min → approx. 4.2 hours/batch

5-batch campaign = 5 × 4.2 h filling
           + 4 h × 4 batch-to-batch changeovers
           + 32 h campaign changeover
           ≈ 85 hours / campaign

blocks.zh: 年產量估算需整合以上所有參數，任何單項假設（如良率、線效率、換線時間）的變動都會顯著影響年批次數。
blocks.en: The annual output estimate must integrate all of the above parameters, and a change in any single assumption (such as yield, line efficiency or changeover time) will significantly affect the number of batches per year.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 100% IPC vs. 統計 IPC 的取捨
blocks.en: Key Point — Trade-off Between 100% IPC and Statistical IPC

blocks.zh: Guide 明確指出：巢式充填機若要做 100% IPC（每支都稱重），充填速率會從「分鐘計百支」掉到「小時計百支」——差距達 100 倍以上。然而，對於高價值 mAb 產品，100% IPC 保護的產品損耗節省，可能超過速度損失的機會成本。決策本質是 產品 CQA（藥品完整性）vs. 商業效率，決策層級 #2 vs. #3。
blocks.en: The Guide states clearly that if a nested filler is to perform 100% IPC (weighing every syringe), the filling rate drops from "hundreds per minute" to "hundreds per hour", a difference of more than 100 times. However, for a high-value mAb product, the product loss avoided by 100% IPC may outweigh the opportunity cost of the lost speed. The decision is essentially product CQA (drug product integrity) vs. commercial efficiency, decision hierarchy #2 vs. #3.

blocks.zh: 若選用蠕動泵 (PP) 並執行 500 L 批次（2.5 百萬支注射器），管路磨損 (hose wear) 為何成為關鍵考量？你會如何在設計中緩解這個問題？
blocks.en: If a peristaltic pump (PP) is selected and a 500 L batch (2.5 million syringes) is run, why does hose wear become a key consideration? How would you mitigate this problem in the design?

blocks.zh: 「線效率 85%」主要靠什麼實現——設備自動化，還是操作員技能？Guide 的觀點是什麼？
blocks.en: What mainly delivers "85% line efficiency": equipment automation or operator skill? What is the Guide's view?

blocks.zh: 21.1.6 Case 1: Comparison of Requirements to Filling System Capabilities (充填技術比較矩陣)
blocks.en: 21.1.6 Case 1: Comparison of Requirements to Filling System Capabilities

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — 矩陣決策法的實際應用
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Practical Application of the Matrix Decision Method

blocks.zh: 本節最重要的學習是「如何用需求矩陣做充填技術決策」。Guide 的結論邏輯：
blocks.en: The most important lesson of this section is "how to use a requirements matrix to make a filling technology decision". The Guide's concluding logic is:

blocks.zh: RPP 首先被排除：剪切敏感性是非談判性紅線，直接淘汰。
blocks.en: RPP is excluded first: Shear sensitivity is a non-negotiable red line, which eliminates it immediately.

blocks.zh: DP 條件性排除：若未來 0.2 mL 小劑量是必要需求，DP 在其能力下限，風險較高。
blocks.en: DP is conditionally excluded: If the 0.2 mL small dose is a required future need, DP is at the lower limit of its capability and the risk is higher.

blocks.zh: PP vs. TP 的最終競爭：
blocks.en: The final contest between PP and TP:

blocks.zh: 若偏好 SU 流路 + 嚴重起泡 → PP 最優
blocks.en: If SU fluid path + severe foaming are preferred → PP is optimal

blocks.zh: 若偏好 CIP/SIP + 精準充填穩定性 → TP 最優
blocks.en: If CIP/SIP + precise fill stability are preferred → TP is optimal

blocks.zh: DP 作為 SU 替代也有競爭力，但體積彈性較弱
blocks.en: DP is also competitive as an SU alternative, but its volume flexibility is weaker

blocks.zh: 這就是決策層級的實踐：無菌保證 (SA) 驅動選擇隔離器；產品 CQA（剪切敏感）驅動排除 RPP；商業彈性（SU vs. CIP/SIP）才決定 PP / TP / DP 的最終選擇。
blocks.en: This is the decision hierarchy in practice: sterility assurance (SA) drives the choice of an isolator; product CQA (shear sensitivity) drives the exclusion of RPP; and commercial flexibility (SU vs. CIP/SIP) determines the final choice among PP / TP / DP.

blocks.zh: 這就像選購廚房主刀：第一步先排除不適合食材的刀型（比如剔骨刀不適合切薄片），第二步在剩下的候選刀中，根據你的使用習慣（慣用日式還是西式、用多久換一次）做最終決定。充填泵的選擇邏輯完全相同——先用產品 CQA 砍掉不相容的選項，再用商業需求做最終比選。
blocks.en: It is like choosing a main kitchen knife: first rule out the knife types that do not suit the ingredients (a boning knife is not suitable for slicing thinly, for example); then, among the remaining candidates, make the final decision based on your habits (Japanese or Western style, how often you replace it). The logic for choosing a filling pump is exactly the same: first use product CQA to eliminate incompatible options, then use commercial requirements to make the final comparison.

blocks.zh: 本案最終選定 PP、TP、DP 為候選，若你是 CDMO 的技術總監，你會選哪一個？請從「5 批活動 × 500 L 批次」的磨損和 SU 成本角度給出理由。
blocks.en: In this case PP, TP and DP were finally selected as candidates. If you were the CDMO's technical director, which would you choose? Give your reasons from the perspective of wear and SU cost for "5-batch campaigns × 500 L batches".

blocks.zh: 「感測充填（sensor filling）與巢式充填機不兼容」這個限制，對未來添加卡匣式容器的計畫有何影響？
blocks.en: What impact does the limitation that "sensor filling is incompatible with nested fillers" have on the plan to add cartridges in the future?

blocks.zh: 21.2 Case 2: Large Volume Parenteral — Liquid in a Bottle (大容量瓶裝液體案例)
blocks.en: 21.2 Case 2: Large Volume Parenteral — Liquid in a Bottle

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — Case 1 vs. Case 2 的關鍵差異
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Key Differences Between Case 1 and Case 2

blocks.zh: Case 2 與 Case 1 有兩個決定性的結構差異：
blocks.en: Case 2 differs from Case 1 in two decisive structural ways:

blocks.zh: 容器類型：從巢式預充填注射器 (nested PFS) 改為傳統散裝瓶 (bulk bottle)，需要玻璃瓶清洗機 + 去熱原隧道 (depyrogenation tunnel)，整個容器供應邏輯完全不同。
blocks.en: Container type: The change from nested prefilled syringes (PFS) to conventional bulk bottles requires a glass bottle washer plus a depyrogenation tunnel, so the whole container supply logic is completely different.

blocks.zh: 充填體積：從 0.5 mL 跳到 250 mL，放大 500 倍。這不僅影響泵型選擇（需要更高流量），也影響充填曲線設計與針頭直徑。
blocks.en: Fill volume: Jumping from 0.5 mL to 250 mL is a 500-fold scale-up. This affects not only pump selection (higher flow rates are needed) but also the fill profile design and needle diameter.

blocks.zh: 環境選擇未定：Case 1 明確選擇隔離器；Case 2 的隔離器 vs. RABS 還在評估。這是商業決策（成本考量）進入設計流程的時機，但前提是兩者都能滿足無菌保證。
blocks.en: Environment choice not yet decided: Case 1 clearly chose an isolator, whereas Case 2 is still evaluating isolator vs. RABS. This is the point at which a commercial decision (cost considerations) enters the design process, but only on the premise that both can meet sterility assurance requirements.

blocks.zh: 相同點：同樣氧敏感、同樣剪切敏感、同樣有起泡傾向——血漿蛋白與 mAb 在物理化學行為上有諸多共通之處。
blocks.en: Similarities: also oxygen-sensitive, also shear-sensitive and also prone to foaming, as plasma proteins and mAbs share many physicochemical behaviors.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 黏度 25 mPa-s 的設計意義
blocks.en: Key Point — The Design Significance of a Viscosity of 25 mPa-s

blocks.zh: Case 2 的黏度（25 mPa-s）遠高於 Case 1 的水狀液體（1-2 mPa-s），但 Guide 明確指出「還不足以限制技術選擇」。通常黏度超過 100-200 mPa-s，充填技術才會受到顯著影響（如需要加熱系統或特殊泵型）。此處教導我們：黏度是設計篩選的連續變數，不是非黑即白的開關。
blocks.en: The viscosity of Case 2 (25 mPa-s) is much higher than that of the water-like liquid in Case 1 (1-2 mPa-s), but the Guide states clearly that it is "not high enough to limit the choice of technology". Typically, filling technology is only significantly affected when viscosity exceeds 100-200 mPa-s (for example, when a heating system or special pump type is needed). This teaches us that viscosity is a continuous variable in design screening, not an on/off switch.

blocks.zh: Case 2 的充填體積是 Case 1 的 500 倍，但充填速率不一定要是 500 倍——為什麼？大容量充填在哪些方面反而讓設計「更簡單」？
blocks.en: The fill volume in Case 2 is 500 times that of Case 1, but the filling rate does not need to be 500 times higher. Why? In what respects does large volume filling actually make the design "simpler"?

blocks.zh: 為什麼 Case 2 的充填環境（隔離器 vs. RABS）還未決定，但 Case 1 已確定使用隔離器？這個差異說明了什麼設計邏輯？
blocks.en: Why has the filling environment (isolator vs. RABS) not yet been decided for Case 2, while Case 1 has already settled on an isolator? What design logic does this difference illustrate?

blocks.zh: 21.2.2–21.2.3 Case 2: Container–Closure Characteristics & Specific Filling Requirements 21.2.2–21.2.3 案例二：容器封蓋特性與特定充填需求
blocks.en: 21.2.2–21.2.3 Case 2: Container–Closure Characteristics & Specific Filling Requirements

blocks.zh: 核心概念 — 散裝線 vs. 巢式線的容器供應差異
blocks.en: Core Concepts — Differences in Container Supply Between Bulk and Nested Lines

blocks.zh: Case 2 使用傳統散裝玻璃瓶 (bulk glass bottle)，沒有 Tub/Nest 系統。這意味著：
blocks.en: Case 2 uses conventional bulk glass bottles, with no tub/nest system. This means:

blocks.zh: 需要在線洗瓶機 (in-line washer) 和去熱原隧道 (depyrogenation tunnel)，設備占地更大。
blocks.en: An in-line washer and a depyrogenation tunnel are needed, and the equipment occupies a larger footprint.

blocks.zh: 玻璃瓶的圓度公差 (roundness control) 是關鍵——圓度不佳的瓶子在傳送帶上容易卡住或傾倒，影響線效率。
blocks.en: Roundness control of the glass bottles is critical: bottles with poor roundness easily jam or topple on the conveyor, affecting line efficiency.

blocks.zh: 軋蓋規格（32 mm Flip Seal，鋁裙長 13 mm）直接決定軋蓋機的壓力設定和線上視覺检查的合格標準。
blocks.en: The crimping specification (32 mm flip seal, 13 mm aluminum skirt length) directly determines the crimping pressure settings and the acceptance criteria for in-line visual inspection.

blocks.zh: 頂空氧含量規格（<4% O₂）是具體的 CQA 目標，設備設計必須確保能穩定達成這個指標。
blocks.en: The headspace oxygen specification (<4% O₂) is a concrete CQA target, and the equipment design must ensure that this target is achieved consistently.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 機械插塞 vs. 真空插塞的選擇
blocks.en: Key Point — Choosing Between Mechanical Stoppering and Vacuum Stoppering

blocks.zh: Case 2 選擇機械插塞 (mechanical stopper-insertion)，理由是：250 mL 大瓶的瓶口夠大（32 mm），插塞力學上不需要真空輔助。但文中要求開發報告證明插塞後不會因壓力彈起 (pop-off)——這是品質風險管理 (QRM) 在關閉操作中的具體體現。相比之下，Case 1 的注射器選用通氣管 (vent tube) 插塞，是因為注射器管徑小，真空不必要但通氣管可輔助排氣。
blocks.en: Case 2 uses mechanical stopper insertion because the neck of the 250 mL bottle is large enough (32 mm) that vacuum assistance is mechanically unnecessary. However, the text requires a development report demonstrating that the stopper will not pop off under pressure after insertion, which is a concrete expression of quality risk management (QRM) in the closing operation. By comparison, the syringe in Case 1 uses vent tube stoppering because the syringe barrel is narrow: vacuum is unnecessary, but the vent tube helps to release air.

blocks.zh: 想像你在裝瓶紅酒：250 mL 的大瓶子（Case 2）可以直接機械壓蓋，軟木塞靠機械力穩穩壓入；但細長的注射器（Case 1）像在幫針筒裝蓋，空間狹小，需要借助通氣管讓空氣排出，才能順利到位。容器幾何形狀決定了關閉方式。
blocks.en: Imagine bottling wine: a large 250 mL bottle (Case 2) can simply be capped mechanically, with the cork pressed firmly in by mechanical force; but a slender syringe (Case 1) is like fitting a cap onto a needle barrel, where space is tight and a vent tube is needed to let the air escape so the stopper can seat properly. Container geometry determines the closing method.

blocks.zh: Case 2 的頂空規格是 <4% O₂。如果你是設備驗收工程師，你會設計哪些測試來證明這個規格能被穩定達成？
blocks.en: The headspace specification for Case 2 is <4% O₂. If you were the equipment acceptance engineer, which tests would you design to demonstrate that this specification can be achieved consistently?

blocks.zh: Case 2 不需要冷藏設計，但 Case 1 需要。這個差異如何影響廠房佈局（clean room 與倉儲銜接）的設計？
blocks.en: Case 2 does not require cold storage design, but Case 1 does. How does this difference affect the design of the facility layout (the link between the cleanroom and warehousing)?

blocks.zh: 本節重點回顧 Section 21A Summary
blocks.en: Section 21A Summary

blocks.zh: 結構化需求矩陣是核心工具：Guide 透過「產品特性 → 容器密封 → 充填要求 → 批次規模 → 技術比較」的五步驟框架，系統性地將產品知識轉化為設備設計決策。
blocks.en: The structured requirements matrix is the core tool: Through a five-step framework of "product characteristics → container closure → filling requirements → batch scale → technology comparison", the Guide systematically converts product knowledge into equipment design decisions.

blocks.zh: 決策層級貫穿每個案例：無菌保證 (SA) 驅動了 Case 1 選擇隔離器的決定（即使產品非高毒性）；產品 CQA（剪切敏感性）排除了 RPP；商業需求（SU vs. CIP/SIP）才決定最終泵型選擇。
blocks.en: The decision hierarchy runs through every case: Sterility assurance (SA) drove the decision to choose an isolator in Case 1 (even though the product is not highly potent); product CQA (shear sensitivity) excluded RPP; and commercial requirements (SU vs. CIP/SIP) determined the final pump type.

blocks.zh: Case 1 vs. Case 2 的設計分歧點：容器格式（巢式 vs. 散裝）、充填體積（0.5 mL vs. 250 mL）、插塞方式（通氣管 vs. 機械），以及充填環境選擇（已確定 vs. 待評估），揭示了不同產品形態如何導向截然不同的設備設計路徑。
blocks.en: Where Case 1 and Case 2 diverge in design: Container format (nested vs. bulk), fill volume (0.5 mL vs. 250 mL), stoppering method (vent tube vs. mechanical) and filling environment choice (decided vs. under evaluation) show how different product formats lead to very different equipment design paths.

blocks.zh: 前瞻彈性是 CDMO 的生命線：從多體積、多容器、多產品的彈性規劃，到填充技術的可擴展性，Guide 反覆強調：初始設計時不考慮未來的決策，日後將以數倍代價彌補。
blocks.en: Forward-looking flexibility is a CDMO's lifeline: From flexible planning for multiple volumes, containers and products to the scalability of filling technology, the Guide repeatedly stresses that decisions made without considering the future at initial design will be paid for many times over later.

blocks.zh: 具體操作指標的實務意義：98% 良率、85% 線效率、70-80% 設備效率、32 小時活動換線——這些數字不是口號，是年度產量計算的基礎，也是 CDMO 對客戶交貨承諾的底層假設。
blocks.en: The practical meaning of specific operating metrics: 98% yield, 85% line efficiency, 70-80% equipment efficiency and a 32-hour campaign changeover: these numbers are not slogans. They are the basis of the annual output calculation and the underlying assumptions behind a CDMO's delivery commitments to its customers.
